concepts.why: The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, and had elevated troponin levels and 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery.
The patient experienced similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes, and had hypomotility in the anterior wall and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 57%.
The patient had a history of hypertension for 5 years, treated with reserpine, and presented with elevated blood pressure.
The patient had 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery and hypomotility in the anterior wall.
The patient presented with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea, and had hypomotility in the anterior wall.
The patient had elevated troponin levels, hypomotility in the anterior wall, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 57%, but did not have ST-segment elevation.

rationales.F01: Acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm is highly suggestive of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F02: Similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously is more indicative of unstable angina.
rationales.F09: Elevated serum troponin I level is a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery is a strong indicator of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F11: Hypomotility in the anterior wall is indicative of myocardial infarction.

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated serum troponin I level and 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery support Acute Myocardial Infarction, with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction as a close runner-up due to the presence of ST-segment elevation in avR and reciprocal ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF.
